conflicts.quote: Verified at source: that primitive is consumed by seven files (`LiveTape`, `TickerDashboard`, `StraddleMove`, `MarketContext`, `IvRank`, `DealerPositioning`, `DealerFlowProjection`) and is re-exported from the shared UI barrel.
conflicts.why: Both halves are falsified by the tree. There are exactly TWO `import { StatTile }` statements in `apps/dashboard/src`: `pages/ticker/widgets/live-tape/LiveTape.tsx:35` and `pages/ticker/widgets/dealer-positioning/DealerPositioning.tsx:25`. Every other match is prose: `TickerDashboard.tsx:5` is a header comment listing widget names; `StraddleMove.tsx:69`, `IvRank.tsx:81`, `MarketContext.tsx:4,152` and `DealerFlowProjection.tsx:67,84` say "the StatTile-family idiom" in comments about a shared *look*, and import nothing. And it is NOT re-exported from the shared UI barrel — `shared/ui/index.ts:15-22` exports ComingSoonBox, ComingSoonBadge/Card, ErrorBoundary, Jargon, Refused, TintChip, ValueCard and `./Widget`, and its own header at `:7-8` says in terms "`StatTile` and the ticker `copy` map stay ticker-local (still one consumer each)". The only barrel that re-exports it is the ticker-local `pages/ticker/widgets/_kit/index.ts:11`. This is not a pedantic count: pm's §2 seam ruling, DS-2's carve-out and AC-22's six-screen scope all price the swap as touching landing, positions, scanner, settings and alerts. It touches none of them — the primitive does not render outside two ticker widgets, so no figure on any of those five screens has a coloured accent edge to delete.
conflicts.proposal: Re-price the sweep as 16 render sites in 2 files (`DealerPositioning` 12, `LiveTape` 4) — a hand-edit, not a codemod — and keep pm's screen-by-screen review list intact but re-attribute what changes on each screen: on landing/positions/scanner/settings/alerts the only visible delta is the radius move (10 → 12) and the token rebind, NOT the figure anatomy. Then AC-22 ("same label and same value after") is trivially true off the ticker page and is a real assertion only on ticker, which is where the review effort should go. If the council wants the accent-bar anatomy provably gone rather than merely unimported, the mechanism is my §8 row: an arc.spec-style source scan asserting `StatTile.tsx` no longer exists and no `accentColor` prop survives anywhere.

conflicts.quote: The desk, scanner, positions, settings, alerts and landing keep their composition; `FigureCell` lands **in place** at every existing `StatTile` call site (`LiveTape` 4 cells, `DealerPositioning` 11–12, `IvRank`, `MarketContext`, `StraddleMove`, `DealerFlowProjection`).
conflicts.why: Same falsification as the pm conflict above, reached independently: `IvRank`, `MarketContext`, `StraddleMove` and `DealerFlowProjection` contain no `StatTile` import. Their references are comments describing a family resemblance — `MarketContext.tsx:152` "the LimbCard-style StatTile-family surface", `DealerFlowProjection.tsx:84` "a StatTile-family surface", `IvRank.tsx:81` "the tooltip carrier — the StatTile-family idiom", `StraddleMove.tsx:69` "matching the StatTile / IvRank idiom". Those four widgets hand-roll their own label/value markup. This matters for ux more than for pm, because it means the F1–F9 state matrix does NOT automatically reach them: a `StatTile → FigureCell` swap leaves four ticker widgets rendering figures that carry no register, no live slot and none of the F5/F7/F8 exclusivity. The register rule would be true of the two swapped widgets and silently false of the four look-alikes on the same page — which is exactly the per-widget convention the brief's Decision impact says this phase exists to close.
conflicts.proposal: Split the surface explicitly and let R4 bind both halves: (a) the 2-file / 16-site swap, where F1–F9 land as component states; and (b) a named, countable list of the four look-alike widgets that will still render un-registered figures after phase 1. Either they are adopted into `FigureCell` in this phase — which is a larger change than 16 sites and should be priced, not assumed — or the SPEC states the gap and the enforcement scan is scoped to the swapped widgets so it is not vacuously green. My preference is (b) plus a stale-entry-checked exemption list naming the four, the `hex-discipline` EXEMPT idiom, so the debt is visible and countable for phase 2 instead of invisible.

conflicts.quote: With a genuinely delivering stream, the page carries **exactly one** liveness claim — counting the chip, any live dot, any pulse and any "live" wording — and that claim reads live and names the mid it is showing.
conflicts.why: As written and marked ship-blocking, AC-1 cannot coexist with the design the other two positions share. ux F3 gives every live-derived figure a live dot in its label row, and ux §4 rules "The dot is per-figure, not per-widget"; my own §3 prop contract has `live?: boolean` driving that dot. On the ticker page with a delivering stream that produces, at minimum: the header chip, the `Widget` livebar (`LiveTape.tsx:130` passes `live={widgetLive}`), and dots on Net flow, Spread and Gamma flip (live). A test "asserting a count of one across the rendered page" fails against the correct implementation. There is a second, independent reason the count is unreliable: `CommandDeck.tsx:196-214` keeps the sticky condensed bar MOUNTED-but-hidden (`aria-hidden={!condensed}`, with the code comment "We keep it MOUNTED-but-hidden vs unmounted to avoid layout jump") and `CommandDeck.tsx:96` calls the shared `connectionChip` resolver, so two chip nodes are attached to the DOM at all times. Any node-counting assertion is wrong in both directions at once.
conflicts.proposal: Scope the count to the claim's own scope, which is what canon rule 18 actually constrains: exactly one PAGE-scoped liveness claim (the chip), at most one WIDGET-scoped bar per widget frame, and a FIGURE-scoped dot only on a figure whose value arrived from a delivering stream. Enforce it as three separate assertions rather than one count: (a) importer set-equality on the connection-chip resolver module, so no surface can mint a second page claim; (b) at most one *visible* chip node — visibility, not attachment, or `CommandDeck`'s hidden bar fails a correct build; (c) the subordinate signals (widget bar, figure dot, tick flash) are all gated on the same `genuineIsLive` predicate the resolver uses, so they cannot outlive the stream. (c) is what AC-11 already wants and it is the assertion that carries the honesty content AC-1 was reaching for.

conflicts.quote: Ruling: **before the first payload the chip shows its loading form; after the first payload some state is always shown.**
conflicts.why: This is refused head-on by ux §3, which writes "A "connecting" chip is the seventh state, and it is banned." and grounds the refusal in the shipped resolver returning `null` at `TickerHeader.tsx:329`. Both are honesty arguments pointing opposite ways and neither is a feasibility question — a loading form is trivially buildable, so the roles cannot settle it between themselves on facts. It also lands on the BRIEF's invariant watch verbatim: `[live-vs-static-isolation]` says "a cold skeleton is not an offline state", and pm's own R-E lists closed and offline as distinct looks — a "connecting" chip sits in the gap between them and is, by construction, a claim about the connection made before any connection fact exists. Architecturally it is not free either: it adds a seventh `kind` to the union my §4 makes exhaustive with a `never` default arm, so the six-state enumeration test and "no seventh reachable" both have to be re-specified around it.
conflicts.proposal: The owner rules. If the answer is pm's, the union becomes seven `kind`s with `loading` reachable only while no stream fact has been observed, the chip must be structurally unable to re-enter `loading` after the first payload (a monotonic latch, not a re-derivation), and the six-state language in the BRIEF and canon rule 18 needs an Amendments line. If the answer is ux's, pm's AC-9 must be rewritten to assert the ABSENCE of a chip before the first fact — which is still a testable claim and still closes pm's risk 1, because the page-level three-degraded-states walk keys on `cold-skeleton` (`StatTile.spec.tsx:32-38`), so the trader is not looking at a silent page, they are looking at a skeleton. My reading is that ux's is the smaller lie, but I hold it weakly and it is not mine to rule.

conflicts.quote: On a stream drop, a live-derived figure keeps its **last known value** at reduced opacity with the pause marker and says it is the last known value — never blanked, never replaced by a zero or a dash.
conflicts.why: This is ship-blocking and it describes behaviour the app does not have. Verified: `LiveTape.tsx:73` sets `numbersActive = isLive && !streamOffline`; `:78` sets `netFlow = numbersActive && live ? live.net_flow : null`; `:140` renders `'—'` when null; `:148` computes spread identically. On a drop the live-derived figures are replaced by a dash today, and `:142`/`:150` still pass `offline={tileOffline}`, so the caption asserts offline beside a dash. ux §8.2 found the same thing and refused to write the caption. Satisfying AC-17 therefore requires a data-flow change in `LiveTape` — a per-field latch holding the last non-null value across the drop — not a primitive swap. That is a behaviour change to a widget on a screen this phase's non-goal 1 says keeps its current composition, and it changes what a trader sees on a drop from "we stopped knowing" to "here is a stale number", which is a claim, not a restyle.
conflicts.proposal: The owner rules on whether phase 1 adds retention. If yes: the mechanism is a `useRef` last-non-null latch per live field in `LiveTape`, cleared on symbol change and on replay arm, and it needs its own AC plus a test that the latched value is not re-flashed by `useFlashOnChange` (it did not change — it stopped arriving). If no: AC-17 must be split along ux's F4/F5 boundary — F4 ("offline · last known") only where a value actually arrived before the drop, F5 (bare `—`, caption `offline`) where none did — and `FigureCell` must derive the caption from whether it holds a retained value rather than from the `offline` flag alone. Either way the `· last known` clause must be data-driven; the one outcome I will argue against in R3 is a caption asserting a retained value beside a dash, which is what a literal AC-17 read of today's data produces.

conflicts.quote: At an unchanged viewport width, a figure in a panel narrower than the compact threshold renders at the compact size, and below the tiny threshold at the tiny size — so the step is driven by the **panel**, not the window. | test | Container-step test holding viewport constant across two panel widths |
conflicts.why: The requirement is right and I want it; the evidence attached to it cannot be produced in the harness pm's own note routes it to. AC-20 is a component/state row, and the harness note assigns those to "the existing jsdom + Testing Library harness". jsdom performs no layout and evaluates no container query, so a jsdom test can neither hold a panel width nor observe a rendered figure size — it would pass with the container rule deleted, which is hollow automation of exactly the kind pm's own risk 3 names. ux reached the same conclusion in §9 and marked that row **review** with "do not fake it with a unit test". This is settleable on facts, which is why it is technical rather than product.
conflicts.proposal: Split AC-20 into two rows with two harnesses, both of which are real. (a) Declaration, jsdom-able and non-vacuous: assert the emitted CSS carries the `@container` at-rule with the 360/280 conditions and the 20/17/15 values, using the shipped idiom at `type-floor.spec.tsx:32-39` that reads the injected emotion rule text. One caveat I will not paper over: that helper does `css.split('.'+cls+'{')[1].split('}')[0]`, which reads the FIRST rule bearing the class, so it needs hardening before it can be trusted to see a hoisted at-rule — I have not run it to confirm which rule stylis emits first. (b) Rendered size, Playwright: set a panel to 340px and 260px at a fixed viewport and read the computed font size. The mechanism underneath both is `theme.containerQueries.down(360)` / `.down(280)` against a NAMED container (`containerName: 'panel'` on the `Widget` body, which already sets `containerType: 'inline-size'` at `Widget.tsx:157`), so a rail nested inside a panel cannot answer the panel's query.

conflicts.quote: On a coarse pointer at 393px, every interactive control on the four product surfaces has an effective hit area of at least 44px in both dimensions.
conflicts.why: This is ship-blocking and it is an app-wide audit wearing a foundations AC. The shipped mechanism is narrower than the claim: `shared/theme/theme.ts:80-102` applies the `@media (pointer: coarse)` 44px `minHeight`/`minWidth` floor to the selector list `button, [role="button"], a` (ux §7 verified this). Controls outside that list — text inputs, `[role="option"]`, `[role="tab"]`, checkbox/switch roots, and anything 44px tall but narrower than 44px wide — are not covered, and "effective hit area in both dimensions" is a stricter test than a min-height floor. I have not measured how many controls on Scanner, Ticker, Positions and Alerts fail it, and I could not this session; that uncertainty is the point. The structural problem is the remedy: when a control on positions or scanner fails, the fix is a layout change to a screen this phase's non-goal 1 and pm's own Out-of-scope list both forbid. So a ship-blocking AC and a declared non-goal can be simultaneously binding and simultaneously unsatisfiable, and the phase discovers it at GATE Q.
conflicts.proposal: The owner rules on which one yields. My recommendation: narrow AC-34 to the controls this phase creates or touches — the palette dialog and its rows, the burger drawer, the nav links, the connection chip if it becomes interactive, and `FigureCell`'s ⓘ button (which ux §7 is correctly making a real focusable control, closing the `StatTile.tsx:180-183` whole-tile hover tooltip) — and land the app-wide sweep as a MEASURED, non-blocking inventory: run the coarse-pointer probe over all four surfaces, record every failing selector in the build report, and fence today's failures in a stale-entry-checked exemption list so new violations red-build and the existing debt is countable for phase 3. That gives the owner a number to rule on instead of a phase that fails at the last gate.

conflicts.quote: This phase adds **exactly one** visually-hidden `aria-live="polite"` region per page, owned by the connection chip — mirroring "one chip per page" so a second region cannot appear.
conflicts.why: The intent is right and the guarantee does not follow from the mechanism, because "owned by the connection chip" does not yield one region per page in this tree. `CommandDeck.tsx:96` calls the shared `connectionChip` resolver for the sticky condensed bar, and `CommandDeck.tsx:196-214` keeps that bar MOUNTED-but-hidden with `aria-hidden={!condensed}` rather than unmounting it, by deliberate design ("to avoid layout jump"). So the ticker page has two chip renderers attached at all times, and a region owned by the chip component is instantiated twice. `aria-hidden` suppresses one of them only while `condensed` is false; once the deck scrolls out, `aria-hidden` goes false on the sticky bar while the hero deck is still mounted and not hidden, and both regions announce the same transition. ux anticipated double-announce from `role="status"` plus a region, but not from double-mounting — this is the same defect arriving by a route the chip component cannot see.
conflicts.proposal: Hoist the region out of the chip: one page-scoped announcer mounted once above both chip renderers (the ticker page shell), fed by the single resolver's output, with the chip renderers carrying no `role="status"` and no region of their own. That keeps ux's "one region per page" true by construction rather than by convention, and it survives `CommandDeck`'s mounted-but-hidden bar and any future condensed/expanded pair. The enforceable form is an assertion that exactly one `aria-live` node exists in the chip path plus the importer set-equality on the resolver module from my §4 — together they make a second announcer a red build rather than a screen-reader-only defect.

conflicts.quote: | **replay** | `replay · {SYMBOL} {Wed Sep 2}` | **outline** | hollow ring | no | The only outlined chip; it names a *stored session*, which is what makes it not a liveness claim. |
conflicts.why: This binds replay to a single label with no standing detail, and pm's AC-8 requires the opposite: "A replay that has **ended**, **faulted**, **dropped**, or is running for a **different symbol** is distinguishable from a currently-playing replay in the chip's own words." One label cannot satisfy that. It also deletes shipped honesty content rather than restyling it: `sessionTapeStanding.ts` produces seven standings (starting, playing, gap, ended, drop, fault, not-this-ticker), the resolver already renders distinct text per standing (`day-replay-mock-adapter.spec.tsx:173` pins `'session tape · starting…'`, `:177` pins `tape 09:35:00 ET`), and `:187,191` assert that `drop` and `ended` do NOT say "Live offline". `[present-is-live-paid-only]` names session-tape standing on replay as a class that is not `present`. Collapsing seven standings into one sentence makes the app say less than it truthfully knows, by way of an honesty rule — pm's risk 2 names this exact failure. This is technical rather than product because the standing IS available at render time (the resolver already has it; nothing new is needed), so the roles can settle it.
conflicts.proposal: Keep six chip STATES and let `replay` carry a closed `standing` that varies only the sentence, never the tone and never the liveness claim: `{ kind: 'replay'; standing: ReplayStanding }` where `ReplayStanding` is the seven-member union already produced by `sessionTapeStanding.ts`. The chip stays outlined, keeps the hollow ring, never pulses and never wears the live dot in any standing — that invariant is what makes the detail free. ux writes the seven sentences (they are copy and they are ux's); I guarantee the union is exhaustively switched with a `never` default arm so an eighth standing is a compile error, and the state-enumeration test walks every `kind` × `standing` fixture and asserts the produced set of `kind`s is exactly six. If ux declines and replay keeps one sentence, pm's AC-8 has to be withdrawn and the four distinctions it protects are deleted — which the owner should see happen rather than have it fall out of a copy table.

conflicts.quote: My rule: at most one *visible* liveness claim per page, enforced in the e2e layer where visibility is real, plus a unit-level assertion that the resolver has exactly one importer set.
conflicts.why: WITHDRAWN. My own R1 §3 gives `FigureCell` a `live?: boolean` prop that "drives the label-row dot only", and ux §4 rules the dot is per-figure. A ticker page with a delivering stream then renders one chip, one `Widget` livebar (`LiveTape.tsx:130`) and up to three figure dots — five visible liveness claims, all of them correct. My rule and my own prop contract contradict each other inside one document, and the rule is the half that is wrong. I stated it while arguing against `TapePulseStrip`'s second PAGE-level claim and over-generalised from that case to every visible signal. Leaving it standing would make pm's AC-1 look supported by two positions when it is supported by none, and would red-build a correct implementation.
conflicts.proposal: Replace it with a scoped rule, which is what canon rule 18 constrains and what ux's three-scopes model already states: exactly one PAGE-scoped liveness claim per page — the chip — enforced by importer set-equality on the resolver module plus a visible-node count of one (visibility, not attachment, because `CommandDeck.tsx:196-214` keeps a second chip mounted-but-hidden by design). Widget bars and figure dots are subordinate scopes, unlimited in number, and every one of them is gated on the same `genuineIsLive` predicate the resolver uses, so none can outlive the stream. `TapePulseStrip.tsx:211-214` is still in scope to remove — not because it is a second visible signal, but because it is a second PAGE-scoped claim.

conflicts.quote: `value: string | NotANumber` where `NotANumber` is the **closed six-member union** from canon rule 24, exported as a type. The cell branches on membership, not on a string match, so a seventh literal is a type error rather than a render bug.
conflicts.why: WITHDRAWN as to the cardinality, and with it the enforcement claim. ux §8.5 is right and I verified it independently: `features/trading/positions/labels.ts:126` exports `NO_BASIS_LABEL = 'no basis'`, and `not provided` / `not recorded` are shipped, spec-asserted literals (`genericOptionRow.spec.tsx:146,171-181,226,247-248,260,277-278`; `fixtures.ts:712-742`), with `PROJECT_CONTEXT.md` §5 `[absent-is-not-none]` citing them as canonical. A six-member union does not make a seventh literal a type error — it makes it a plain `string`, which falls through my own `string` branch straight into the mono figure register. So the mechanism I offered as the enforcement of `[ai-asserted-numbers-are-traceable]` would, on the phase-3 positions surface, render a not-a-number word in the "Convexa computed this" face: the exact inversion it was designed to prevent. That is a worse failure than the one I was guarding against, and it is invisible in a green suite.
conflicts.proposal: Keep the union closed — do not take ux's alternative of letting the caller classify, because caller-declared classification returns `[absent-is-not-none]` to prose and defeats `[structural-over-prose-enforcement]`. Instead make it ONE exported type, seeded from the shipped literals rather than from a number: a single `NotANumber` union living beside `[absent-is-not-none]`'s other consumers, whose members are the canon's six plus `not recorded`, `no basis`, `not provided`, with `NO_BASIS_LABEL` and the broker labels re-pointed at it so there is one source of truth instead of four. `FigureCell` branches on that union; adding a member is one edit in one place; a stray string is still not a member. Whether the canon's rule 24 list becomes nine or the three shipped members are retired is an Amendments call for the owner, not a build decision — and pm's AC-19 ("the member count is six") should be re-marked to bind `FigureCell`'s own set until that ruling lands, or it asserts something false about the app.

conflicts.quote: If the palette wants recent tickers, that is a new `convexa.*` key and therefore a `[loss-free-durable-migration]` surface — my position is **defer it**: ship the palette without recents in phase 1.
conflicts.why: WITHDRAWN — the premise is false and I did not check it before asserting it. The durable store already ships: `pages/ticker/recentTickers/store.ts:9` holds `convexa.recent-tickers.v1`, `:78` exports `listRecents()` (MRU, ≤8, de-duped against the closed pins `SPY · QQQ · NVDA`), `:86` exports `recordVisit()`, `:97` exports a test seam, and `PROJECT_CONTEXT.md` records it as shipped 2026-08-11 with the Command Deck QUICK row as its consumer. It also already fails safe: corrupt or unreadable input yields an empty in-memory shape and deliberately does NOT `removeItem`, so the original blob survives (`:61-64`). Reading it from the palette introduces no new key, no new shape, and no schema change — `[loss-free-durable-migration]` never fires. The real cost is a module promotion out of `pages/ticker/` under the repo's "populate `shared/` on the 2nd consumer" rule, because the palette lives in the shell and `pages/` is not the shell's to import. That is a file move plus two import edits.
conflicts.proposal: Drop my deferral. My non-goal 6 stands in its first half — no NEW durable client store and no change to any existing durable key or shape — and I withdraw the recents clause. If the council wants recents in the palette (ux P2 does), the mechanism is: promote `recentTickers/store.ts` to `shared/` (or `features/`) unchanged, call `listRecents()` on open, and add nothing durable. Whether phase 1 SPENDS that is still a scope call and not mine — pm future-dated "recent history" and is entitled to; I am only removing the cost argument I supplied for it, which was wrong.

conflicts.quote: **A "connecting" chip is the seventh state, and it is banned.**
conflicts.why: This makes 'the page carries no liveness claim at all' a shipped and TESTED outcome before the first stream fact, and my R-B/AC-9 rule the opposite. A trader returning to a desk cannot distinguish 'we have not been told yet' from 'everything is fine' — absence reads as fine, which is the single failure US-2 exists to prevent. It is also the one acceptance criterion in this phase that cannot be verified as written: an AC whose observable is 'nothing is on the page' passes identically when the resolver is correct, when it throws, and when the stream never opened. The invariant cited forbids showing OFFLINE during a cold start; it does not forbid stating that we are still connecting.
conflicts.proposal: Owner rules between (a) the chip renders a neutral connecting/loading form until the first stream fact, or (b) the page carries no chip until then. If (b) wins, the criterion must be restated as a positive observable — every surface that will carry a chip shows a placeholder in the chip's place until the first fact — so absence is distinguishable from breakage by a human and by a test. AC-9 stands or falls on that ruling; I will not certify a criterion whose evidence is an empty region.

conflicts.quote: On a stream drop, a live-derived figure keeps its **last known value** at reduced opacity with the pause marker and says it is the last known value — never blanked, never replaced by a zero or a dash.
conflicts.why: WITHDRAWN. UX read at source that on a drop Net flow and Spread render the bare absence literal, not a retained figure, because they are recomputed as null whenever the stream is not delivering. AC-17 as written therefore demands a behaviour change — value retention across a drop — that neither the BRIEF nor my own scope ruling bought, and that my own framing of this phase ('this phase ships no new capability') excludes. I cannot defend an AC that requires the app to start doing something new while calling the phase foundations.
conflicts.proposal: Split into two criteria so the degraded arms stand on their own: (i) a figure that DID receive a value before the drop shows that value dimmed with the pause marker and says it is the last known value; (ii) a figure that had no value at the drop shows the bare absence literal with the pause marker and says only that it is offline — never 'last known'. Then the owner rules separately whether phase 1 pays to move Net flow and Spread from (ii) into (i). Until that ruling, (ii) is the binding state for those two figures and no criterion may assert retention for them.

conflicts.quote: Each of the six not-a-number literals renders as small Sans text, never as a figure, and never substitutes for another member; the member count is six.
conflicts.why: WITHDRAWN in part. UX reports, and I confirmed at source, that the shipped app already renders at least three absence literals beyond the canon's six — `not recorded`, `no basis`, `not provided` — asserted by existing specs on the positions and broker surfaces, two of them cited as canonical in the project context. An AC that fixes the member count at six is either unsatisfiable against shipped code or satisfiable only by deleting shipped literals from screens this phase promised not to touch. My R-H ('no new absence word') survives; 'the member count is six' does not.
conflicts.proposal: Keep the observable half — every absence literal renders as small Sans text, never in the figure register, never substituting for another member — and drop the count from the criterion. Reconciling the canon's list against the shipped set is an owner Amendment, not a build decision; until it lands, the figure primitive must classify the literal from what the caller declares rather than from a fixed six-member list, or phase 3 renders `not recorded` in the face that means 'Convexa computed this'.

conflicts.quote: **No burn-down of the pre-existing spacing/radius debt** beyond making it visible and fenced (§2).
conflicts.why: This is presented as build containment but it is a scope decision, and it contradicts the same position's own radius mechanism. §2 requires a per-site read of roughly two dozen bare-number radius sites because the numeric form re-scales by 1.2x, and risk 3 says the result 'will visibly change surfaces this phase claims not to touch'. So radius debt IS being burned down in part while spacing debt (86 sites across 35 files) is grandfathered with no expiry — and as one sentence it would let a build lane skip the radius sites and still claim the non-goal was honoured. Whether 'foundations' means the app is ON the declared scales or only that new code is fenced from leaving them is a value call the owner is entitled to make, especially since the architect states the M estimate depends on the answer.
conflicts.proposal: Route as two separate owner calls, not one. (1) Spacing: accept a seeded 35-file exemption list as the phase-1 deliverable, with the occurrence count recorded in the build report and a named later phase that burns it down — or reject it and re-price the phase. (2) Radius: the migration is IN, and every site whose radius changes must be enumerated in the change so the per-screen and per-overlay sign-off has a list to check against rather than a reviewer's memory.

conflicts.quote: The migration surface is far smaller than it looks.
conflicts.why: True for the component swap — I verified only two files import the primitive, which falsifies my own R1's count of seven — but not for what the phase must DELIVER. Four widgets on the same ticker page (IvRank, DealerFlowProjection, MarketContext, StraddleMove) are 'StatTile-family' lookalikes that are not importers, and at least two of them wrap a non-focusable info icon in a hover-only tooltip (`IvRank.tsx:91`, `DealerFlowProjection.tsx:77`). If the sweep stops at the two importers, phase 1 ships a page where half the figure cards answer the info affordance to a keyboard or touch user and half do not — and my AC-35, which names the info affordance explicitly, would have to be certified as passing on a page where it demonstrably fails.
conflicts.proposal: Owner rules whether phase 1 pays to give every figure-card info affordance on the ticker page a tap and focus path, or whether AC-35 narrows explicitly to the new primitive's own affordance with the remaining hover-only cards named in the build report as accepted, carried debt with a phase attached. Either is defensible. Shipping the split silently is not, because the reviewer sees a page where the tooltips work under a mouse.

conflicts.quote: **UX will specify the label row as: caps label, info affordance, live dot — and nothing else.**
conflicts.why: UX did not, and on the evidence could not. It found that Call wall and Put wall are distinguished today only by the directional colour this phase deletes, that the caption's sign is distance from spot rather than the wall's side, and ruled a replacement mark is required in phase 1. conflicts.quote: On a stream drop, a live-derived figure keeps its **last known value** at reduced opacity with the pause marker and says it is the last known value — never blanked, never replaced by a zero or a dash.
conflicts.why: Verified at source: not one of the four live-derived cells does this today. LiveTape.tsx:78 computes `const netFlow = numbersActive && live ? live.net_flow : null` and :140 renders the `—` literal; :148 does the same for Spread; :87 makes Gamma flip fall back to the *bundle's* static `m.gamma_flip`, which is a different number, not a retained stream value; :163-168 VWAP takes no `offline` prop at all. So AC-17 certifies a retention the code does not perform, and its "says it is the last known value" clause would print `— · ⏸ offline · last known` — a caption asserting a value the data does not support. That is precisely the failure my lane exists to prevent, and I will not write that string. Making AC-17 true is a behaviour change to LiveTape's data flow, which is scope, not copy.
conflicts.proposal: Split it and let the owner rule the behaviour half. (a) Retention IN: it gets its own AC naming LiveTape's net flow and spread as the changed behaviour, and my F4 becomes the binding offline state for them. (b) Retention OUT: AC-17 is rewritten data-driven — the `· last known` clause renders only when a value actually arrived before the drop (F4); a cell with no retained value renders the bare `—` with `offline` and no `last known` clause (F5); and "never replaced by ... a dash" is dropped, because a dash is the shipped truth. Either way F4 and F5 must be distinguishable in the DOM, not only to the eye.

conflicts.quote: With a genuinely delivering stream, the page carries **exactly one** liveness claim — counting the chip, any live dot, any pulse and any "live" wording — and that claim reads live and names the mid it is showing.
